segments: Why must plaintext secrets stay out of the Store?
In NixOS, configuration sources and files referenced by builds may be copied into /nix/store.
/nix/store is world-readable.
Any ordinary user can find your plaintext API key in /nix/store.
A modern solution: sops-nix
sops-nix provides runtime secret decryption for NixOS and Home Manager.
1. How it works
Encrypt secrets.yaml using age public-key recipients or another method supported by SOPS. The corresponding private keys are used for decryption and kept outside the Store and public repositories.
In Nix, reference only the encrypted file.
The NixOS module decrypts secrets into /run/secrets/ during activation or a service phase. Use owner/group/mode to control which services or users can read them.
2. Practical steps
Install the sops command-line tool.
Generate an age key.

Integrate it into the configuration:
# flake.nix 加入 inputs.sops-nix
# configuration.nix
{ inputs, ... }: {
  imports = [ inputs.sops-nix.nixosModules.sops ];
  sops.defaultSopsFile = ./secrets.yaml;
  sops.age.sshKeyPaths = [ "/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key" ];
  
  # 定义一个密钥
  sops.secrets."github_token" = {};
}
Another option: agenix
agenix is lighter-weight than sops-nix. It manages secrets as individual age files and supports age recipient types, including supported SSH keys.
Using secrets in Home Manager

The NixOS module can decrypt secrets for system services, while user configuration references only runtime file paths and explicitly sets read permissions. sops-nix also provides a Home Manager module that uses a user service to decrypt secrets into a runtime directory. User services that depend on those secrets must be ordered correctly. Do not use builtins.readFile to insert decrypted plaintext into Nix configuration, and do not put secret values in home.sessionVariables. Prefer the application’s credential-file options.
Preparing to publish configuration
If you plan to open-source your Nix configuration, the first step is to remove all passwords and tokens and introduce sops-nix.
Summary
Do not write plaintext passwords in .nix files.
Use appropriate encryption recipients and protect the decryption private keys.
Ensure that private keys and original plaintext never enter Git, the Store, or logs. .gitignore cannot remove leaked content from history that has already been tracked.
